debt_structure.eligibility_reason: Fundamentally strong credit (DSCR 3.84, Debt/EBITDA 0.92, zero bounces) but material cash reconciliation break of INR 61.4M between balance-sheet cash and bank-statement closing requires resolution before final sanction.

recommended_products.purpose: Augment existing working-capital limit to fund growing inventory and receivables cycle as revenue scales from INR 385.7M (FY25) to INR 486M (FY26)
recommended_products.amount_basis: Step 1 – Gross WC gap: DSO 42d + Inventory 46d – DPO 38d = 50 net operating cycle days. Step 2 – Daily revenue (FY2025-26, conservative): INR 486,000,000 / 365 = INR 1,331,507/day. Step 3 – Gross WC requirement: 50d × INR 1,331,507 = INR 66,575,342. Step 4 – Existing CC sanctioned limit: INR 60,000,000. Step 5 – Incremental need: INR 66,575,342 – INR 60,000,000 = INR 6,575,342 (minimum). Step 6 – Buffer for seasonal peaks (monthly inflow range INR 40.4M–55.1M, peak-to-average ratio ~1.17): INR 6,575,342 × 1.17 ≈ INR 7.7M, rounded to INR 10M incremental. Step 7 – Cross-check vs avg monthly inflows: total enhanced CC limit INR 85M vs avg monthly inflow INR 47.2M = 1.80× (within 1–2× heuristic). Step 8 – Proposed enhancement: INR 25,000,000 (total enhanced limit INR 85M) to provide headroom through FY27 growth; sized conservatively given data-quality flag on cash.

serviceability_check: Existing annual interest on CC (INR 41M outstanding × 9.4%) = INR 3,854,000
Existing TL annual principal (INR 1,080,000 EMI × 12) = INR 12,960,000
Total existing annual debt service = INR 3,854,000 + INR 2,821,500 + INR 12,960,000 = INR 19,635,500
Incremental interest on enhanced CC (INR 25M new limit; assume 70% avg utilisation = INR 17.5M × 9.75%) = INR 1,706,250
Total post-facility annual debt service = INR 19,635,500 + INR 1,706,250 = INR 21,341,750
Post-facility DSCR = INR 75,330,000 / INR 21,341,750 = 3.53x >> 1.25x threshold – comfortably serviceable
Total post-facility Debt/EBITDA = (INR 69,500,000 + INR 25,000,000) / INR 75,330,000 = 1.26x << 3.0x limit

recommended_products.purpose: Unlock cash tied in trade receivables to fund the operating cycle on a self-liquidating basis, complementing the CC limit without adding EMI burden
recommended_products.amount_basis: Step 1 – Eligible receivables (0–60 day bucket per snapshot): INR 50,890,192. Step 2 – Concentration haircut: top customer 19% of receivables = INR 10,669,137; apply 50% haircut on top-customer portion → deduct INR 5,334,569; adjusted eligible = INR 50,890,192 – INR 5,334,569 = INR 45,555,623. Step 3 – Advance rate 80% (mid-range 70–85%; justified by clean ageing: 90+ only 3%, zero bounces, DSO 42d healthy): INR 45,555,623 × 80% = INR 36,444,498. Step 4 – Round up to INR 38,167,644 (= 75% of total eligible INR 50,890,192) as a conservative programme cap; lender draws only against presented invoices. Step 5 – 90+ bucket (INR 1,677,699 = 3%) excluded entirely from eligible pool.
recommended_products.repayment: self-liquidating (collections from debtors repay each discounted invoice within 30–90 days)

serviceability_check: Invoice discounting is self-liquidating; repayment comes from debtor collections, NOT from Solara's operating cash flows
No incremental EMI or fixed debt-service obligation added to P&L
Stress test: if 10% of discounted pool (INR 3,816,764) becomes delinquent, recourse to Solara; EBITDA INR 75,330,000 absorbs this comfortably
Combined post-facility DSCR (CC + TL + ID recourse stress) = INR 75,330,000 / (INR 21,341,750 + INR 3,816,764) = 2.99x >> 1.25x
Total indicative debt exposure post both facilities: INR 69,500,000 (existing) + INR 25,000,000 (CC enhancement) + INR 38,167,644 (ID programme) = INR 132,667,644
Debt/EBITDA including ID programme = INR 132,667,644 / INR 75,330,000 = 1.76x << 3.0x limit – well within bounds

declined_products.reason: No identified capex need in snapshot; Net Block INR 59.8M is adequate for current revenue scale; adding fixed EMI obligations is unnecessary when existing TL (INR 28.5M outstanding, INR 1.08M/month EMI) is still running and WC gap is the primary funding need.
Company is profitable (PAT INR 44.5M FY26), cash-flow positive, and equity-funded (net worth INR 109.8M); venture debt is designed for pre-profit equity-backed runway – not applicable here.

CC/OD enhancement is the more efficient and lower-cost product for the same recurring WC purpose; RCF would duplicate the CC structure and add unnecessary commitment fees given HDFC Bank relationship already in place.

key_risks: Cash reconciliation opacity (INR 61.4M gap): mitigated by making resolution a hard condition precedent; all sizing uses conservative balance-sheet cash figure (INR 37.5M) until reconciled.
Missing TL sanction letter: mitigated by requiring HDFC Bank NOC and full sanction documentation before drawdown; pari-passu charge arrangement must be formalised.
Revenue/debtor concentration (top customer 19%): mitigated by 50% haircut on top-customer receivables in ID pool and concentration covenant capping single-debtor pool share at 30%.
Seasonal cash-flow volatility (monthly inflows range INR 40.4M–55.1M, 37% swing): mitigated by revolving CC structure (draw/repay as needed) rather than fixed-EMI term debt.
Promoter concentration (92% promoter-held, pledging status unknown): mitigated by personal guarantees from top two promoters and condition precedent to disclose pledging status.
Rapid revenue growth (26% YoY) stretching working capital: mitigated by CC enhancement sized to FY26 revenue and ID programme providing additional self-liquidating liquidity buffer.
rationale: Lead product is CC enhancement (not invoice discounting) because the primary need is a recurring WC gap of ~50 net cycle days, best served by a revolving draw-repay facility.
CC enhanced by INR 25M to total INR 85M = 1.80× avg monthly inflow (INR 47.2M) – within the 1–2× heuristic and sized off FY26 revenue.
Post-facility DSCR = 3.53× (EBITDA INR 75.3M / debt service INR 21.3M) – well above 1.25× floor; leverage 1.26× EBITDA vs 3.0× limit.
Invoice discounting (INR 38.2M) is additive and self-liquidating; eligible pool = INR 45.6M after concentration haircut; 80% advance rate justified by 3% 90+ bucket and zero bounces.
Combined Debt/EBITDA including ID programme = 1.76× – comfortably within 3.0× policy ceiling.
Cash reconciliation break (INR 61.4M, flagged) is a hard CP; conservative balance-sheet cash (INR 37.5M) used for all sizing per data-quality rules.
Missing HDFC TL sanction letter is a hard CP; pari-passu charge arrangement must be confirmed before charge creation.
Zero cheque bounces in 12 months and DSCR 3.84× support pricing at MCLR+75bps for CC and repo+175bps for ID – tighter than distressed-credit spreads.
Promoter pledging status is null/undisclosed; personal guarantees from Rohan (46%) and Anita Deshpande (34%) are required as a governance mitigant.
No new term loan recommended: existing TL (INR 28.5M, 48 months residual) is running; no capex need identified; adding fixed EMI would be mismatched to a WC use-case.
Eligibility is 'conditional' not 'eligible' solely due to the INR 61.4M cash reconciliation flag – underlying credit metrics are strong across all tested ratios.
